# dlgskill


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Use this whenever the question or edit concerns a notebook’s content:
messages, sources, outputs, prompts and their replies.

## The hierarchy

Notebook work happens at three levels, and picking the right level is
most of using this module well:

- Content (this module): what the messages say and how they change.
  [`summary_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#summary_dlg),
  [`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#find_msgs),
  [`view_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#view_dlg),
  the message editing operations.
- Representation (`fastcore.nbio`): which keys exist, whether a file is
  schema-valid, whether bytes changed. Start with
  `validate_nb`/`validate_cell`, which name the cell at fault; use
  `read_nb` directly when the question is about the dict itself. For
  *plain* notebooks (no dialog semantics), nbio’s `Notebook`/`NbCell`
  objects and `cell_*` functions are the content surface, and this
  module’s word choice marks the layer: cells for notebooks, messages
  for dialogs.
- Raw text: only when the file will not parse at all.

## Core APIs

The function/method two-shapes contract is `fastcore.editskill`’s,
learned once: the function is a transaction addressed by `dlg=` (an
ipynb path, or None meaning the current dialog file:
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg));
the method is a session on a held
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog) or
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message),
saved by an explicit `dlg.save()` (`msg_str_replace(id, ..., dlg=p)` ⟷
`m.str_replace(...)`). Wrapping any message list in an ephemeral
`Dialog(msgs)` makes the whole session surface available on it.

- `summary_dlg(dlg)` / `d.summary()`: one `preview` per message,
  `id:t[directives]:content` (t: c=code n=note p=prompt r=raw; the
  bracket, as in nbio’s `CellRow`, shows meta-form nbdev directives such
  as `[export]`), with a prompt’s reply on a following `>` line; a line
  cut short ends in a humanized `[size]`.
- `find_msgs(pattern, dlg, ...)`: search by regex, type, errors,
  heading, ids, or a `pred`
  ([`symdef_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#symdef_finder)/[`symref_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#symref_finder)/[`ast_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#ast_finder)
  build structural ones); `context` defaults to 1 even with `ids=`,
  because the neighbouring message usually explains the match – retrieve
  and read it. Returns
  [`MsgRow`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgrow)
  snapshots (`id`, `msg_type`, `content`, `out`, `meta`) in a
  [`MsgRows`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgrows);
  `d.find_msgs(...)` returns live
  [`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)s
  in a
  [`FoundMsgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#foundmsgs).
  Both index by message id (exact or unique prefix) and refuse integer
  positions: a find result includes context rows, so `[0]` may be a
  neighbour of the match, and the raised error teaches the id idiom.
  Previews mark context rows with `-` in place of the first `:`. Every
  live message carries a `dlg` backref to its owning
  [`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog),
  so dialog-level operations are always in reach from a message in hand
  (e.g. `m.dlg.save()` after mutating `m.output` directly).
- `view_dlg(dlg)` / `d.view()` / `view_msg(id)` / `m.view()` /
  `view_msgs(*ids)` / `msg2xml(m)` / `m.to_xml()`: full views in the
  shared `item2xml` grammar (a prompt’s reply is its `<out>` section;
  meta `nbdev` directives render as attrs, so a meta-exported message
  carries a bare `export`); `incl_out=True` on the line views appends
  the message’s output the same way.
- Structure:
  [`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg),
  [`del_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#del_msgs),
  [`move_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#move_msgs),
  [`split_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#split_msg),
  [`merge_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#merge_msgs),
  [`copy_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#copy_msgs)/[`cut_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#cut_msgs)/[`paste_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#paste_msgs),
  [`create_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#create_dlg),
  with session twins `d.move_msgs`, `m.split`, `d.merge_msgs`,
  `d.copy_msgs`/`d.cut_msgs`/`d.paste_msgs` (session adds go through
  `d.mk_message`, deletes through `d.remove_msgs`).
  [`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg)
  with neither `before=` nor `after=` places after the current message
  ([`set_cur_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_cur_msg),
  which a host sets and no write ever moves), or at the end when that is
  unset or gone.
  [`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg)
  and `d.mk_message` take `meta=` and an `export=` shortcut for the meta
  `nbdev` export flag, readable and assignable as `m.meta_exported`
  (`m.exported` reads content and meta together, and is what
  `find_msgs(only_exp=True)` filters on). The `%%add_msg` magic takes
  its body verbatim: its line is
  `%%add_msg [dlg] [msg_type] [export] [before=|after=<id>]`, where a
  bare path token is the dlg and a bare type name the msg_type, and
  keyword spellings win over bare tokens.
- `update_msg(id, ..., dlg=)` / `m.update(...)`: one transaction for a
  message’s attributes. Plain keywords assign (`content=`, `msg_type=`,
  `output=`, `meta=` replacing wholesale); `mergemeta` deep-merges into
  `meta` (a `None` value deletes its key); `export` sets the nbdev
  directive – `True` adds, `False` removes (there is no negative form),
  and either migrates a content-form `#| export` line to meta. The
  function returns a diff of the message’s XML plus a `meta:` line, so
  every change it can make is visible.
- The `%nbrun` line magic runs code cells from the current notebook in
  the running kernel, by cell id prefix, same grammar: bare tokens are
  flags (`above`, `below`, `all`, `exported`, `ignore_eval`,
  `continue_on_error`, `show`) or id prefixes, and `fname=` overrides
  the notebook for one call. Only cells named by id display their
  output: bulk-selected cells run silently (`show` overrides), errors
  always surface naming the failed cell, and the run ends with a
  `nbrun: N cells ok` line. It returns a coroutine (awaited by
  async-magic machinery) and runs each cell in the kernel’s namespace
  through user-level channels only (exec, `display()`, raising), so it
  behaves identically in every kernel.
- `d.execute(*ids, ...)` / `m.execute()`: the captured twin, on a held
  [`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog).
  Runs code messages on an execnb `CaptureShell` (fresh and dropped,
  unless you pass `shell=`), assigns each result to `m.output` in memory
  (`d.save()` persists), and returns the messages run as a
  [`RunResult`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#runresult)
  whose repr is a status report: ok lines collapse into a counted
  marker, failures always show with the exception. It blocks until done,
  so an async host should wrap it in `asyncio.to_thread`.
  `above`/`below` anchor at the ids you pass, and bare `d.execute()`
  runs all participating code messages (the `eval` cascade).
- Text edits: `msg_str_replace`, `msg_strs_replace`, `msg_insert_line`,
  `msg_replace_lines`, `msg_del_lines`, `msg_ast_replace` (all with
  `re_filter`/line-range powers; `out=True` edits a prompt’s reply or a
  code message’s outputs literal), with the same names as
  [`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
  methods for in-memory editing;
  [`lnhashview_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#lnhashview_msg)/[`msg_exhash`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#msg_exhash)
  (and `m.lnhashview()`/`m.exhash()`) for hash-verified line edits
  ([`lnhashview_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#lnhashview_msg)
  is `view_msg(..., lnhashs=True)`; only the exhash pair needs the
  `exhash` package).

## Idiomatic usage

Start by registering the notebook: `set_dlg(path)` makes every function
here default to it (and the `%nbrun` magic follows suit), so calls read
as “do this to message X”. Then orient before acting:

- [`summary_dlg()`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#summary_dlg)
  first for anything sizable: a cheap one-line-per-message map.
  [`view_dlg()`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#view_dlg)
  when you need the full story in order with ids. Read a notebook in
  full before describing or changing what it does - the interleaved
  prose, examples, and stored outputs (`incl_out=True`) are the design
  rationale.
- Read before trying things out: an ad-hoc “what happens if…” check
  usually re-derives, more slowly and less reliably, what an existing
  example cell already shows. If after reading you still need to try it,
  that’s a gap in the notebook - add it as a proper example cell so the
  next reader doesn’t repeat it.
- [`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#find_msgs)
  is the targeted view: keep the default `context=1` (the neighbouring
  markdown usually explains the match), and `ids=` with context is the
  positional query (“does A precede B?”, “what’s the idiom around
  here?”). Name questions are structural, not textual:
  [`symdef_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#symdef_finder)/[`symref_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#symref_finder)/[`ast_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#ast_finder)
  beat regexes over binding syntax. Where available, rgapi’s `nbrg`
  searches cell sources across files and returns the cell ids these
  functions take.
- Edit at the right level:
  [`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg)/`%%add_msg`
  for new messages; within a message, prefer hash-verified addressing
  ([`lnhashview_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#lnhashview_msg)/[`msg_exhash`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#msg_exhash),
  or exhash’s `lnhashview_cell`/`cell_exhash` by path and cell id) -
  view with the lnhash variant the moment an edit is plausible, so the
  view doubles as the edit’s address book. The plain `msg_*` editors fit
  where exhash can’t express the edit, e.g. one `msg_str_replace` across
  an id list. Never splice via `read_nb`/`write_nb` internals: if a
  primitive is missing here, stop and propose adding it.
- `dlg.validate()` catches structural problems early; `dlg.save()`
  writes back. Don’t wrap calls in `hasattr` or `try/except` - call
  directly and read the bare result.

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
from fastcore.tools import lnhash
from tempfile import mkdtemp
from IPython.core.interactiveshell import InteractiveShell
```

### set_dlg

``` python
def set_dlg(
    fname, # ipynb path that later calls will default to
    cls:NoneType=None, # `Dialog` subclass to read with from now on (None: keep current; initially `Dialog`)
):
```

*Set the current dialog file, used by these functions when `dlg` is
None*

[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg)
and
[`set_cur_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_cur_msg)
are how a host tells these functions where the user is: which dialog
file, and which message within it. A host such as Solveit sets the
message as it runs one, so a bare
[`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg)
lands under the prompt being answered. Nothing here ever moves that
anchor, and
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg)
clears it since an id belongs to one file. An anchor that is unset, or
names a message since deleted, is not an error: placement falls back to
the end of the dialog.
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg)
also carries the third host default, `cls=`: the
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
subclass every ambient read constructs, so a host’s own message fields
(declared via `meta_attrs`) are live on everything these functions
return. The class persists across
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg)
calls until replaced, so hopping between files keeps the host’s
semantics.

The stored state is itself public: `cur_msgid` and `cur_dlg_path` are
module attributes holding the bare id and path. They are rebound on
every set, so read them as `dlgskill.cur_msgid`, never via
`from ... import`, which copies the value at import time; for the same
reason they stay out of `__all__`.

### Dialog.msg

``` python
def msg(
    id, # A `Message` (matched by its id), or an id: exact, or unique prefix
):
```

*The matching
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
in this dialog*

On-disk cell ids are message ids without the leading underscore, so
`msg` accepts either form, and unique prefixes work like everywhere else
in this ecosystem. The fixture below is written to disk too, since
path-based calls re-read the file per call:

``` python
tdir = Path(mkdtemp())
d = Dialog(name='demo')
setup = d.mk_message('# Setup', msg_type=snote)
calc = d.mk_message('x = 21\nx*2', msg_type=scode, output=code_output('42'))
ask = d.mk_message('Double it.', msg_type=sprompt, output='It is **42**.')
bad = d.mk_message('1/0', msg_type=scode, output=[dict(output_type='error', ename='E', evalue='boom', traceback=['tb'])])
write_ipynb(d, tdir/'demo.ipynb')
test_eq(d.msg(calc.id), calc)
test_eq(d.msg(calc.id[:5]), calc)  # unique prefixes work too
with expect_fail(KeyError, 'no message'): d.msg('zzzz')
```

``` python
def view_msg(
    id, # Message id, looked up in `dlg` (unique prefixes allowed)
    dlg:NoneType=None, # An ipynb path (expands `~`); the current dialog file if None
    nums:bool=True, # Show line numbers?
    start_line:int=1, # Starting line to view
    end_line:int=None, # End line (defaults to last line if None; -1 for EOF)
    lnhashs:bool=False, # Show exhash `lineno|hash|` addresses instead of line numbers?

    trunc_out:bool=True, # Truncate an included output to ~512 chars?
):
```

*Show a message’s content with optional line numbers or exhash
addresses*

``` python
test_eq(str(calc.view()), '1: x = 21\n2: x*2')
test_eq(str(calc.view(start_line=2)), '2: x*2')
test_eq(str(calc.view(lnhashs=True)), f'{lnhash(1, "x = 21")}x = 21\n{lnhash(2, "x*2")}x*2')
assert str(view_msgs(setup.id, calc.id, dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', nums=False)).startswith(f"# msg {setup.id}")
test_eq(str(view_msgs(calc.id, dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', start_line=2)), f'# msg {calc.id}\n2: x*2')
test_eq(str(calc.view(incl_out=True)), '1: x = 21\n2: x*2\n<out>\n42\n</out>')
assert 'It is **42**.' in str(ask.view(nums=False, incl_out=True))
assert '<out>' not in str(calc.view())
assert '<out>' in str(view_msg(calc.id, dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', incl_out=True))
test_eq(str(view_msgs(calc.id, ask.id, dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', incl_out=True)).count('<out>'), 2)
```

## Searching

[`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#find_msgs)
keeps `context=1` by default even when filtering by `ids=`, because the
neighbouring note usually explains the match – retrieving and reading
that context is the point. What it refuses is *addressing* by position:
a context row can sit at any index, so `fm[0]` may be a neighbour of the
match, and integer indexing raises an error teaching the id idiom. Index
results by message id (exact or unique prefix), which you type yourself,
so a wrong target fails loudly:

### find_msgs

``` python
def find_msgs(
    re_pattern:str='', # Regex over content (a prompt's reply included), DOTALL+MULTILINE; an invalid regex matches literally
    dlg:NoneType=None, # An ipynb path (expands `~`); the current dialog file if None
    msg_type:str=None, # Optional limit by type ('code', 'note', 'prompt', or 'raw')
    only_err:bool=False, # Only code messages with error outputs?
    only_exp:bool=False, # Only exported messages (nbdev export directive in content or meta)?
    ids:str='', # Optionally filter by ids (comma-separated str, or list); results are always in dialog order, whatever order the ids are given
    before:int=0, # Also include n messages before each match
    after:int=0, # Also include n messages after each match
    context:int=None, # Messages of context around matches (default 1, or 0 when `headers_only`)
    limit:int=None, # Max matched messages
    use_case:bool=False, # Case-sensitive matching?
    use_regex:bool=True, # Regex matching (else plain substring)?
    headers_only:bool=False, # Only heading notes (an outline view)?
    header_section:str=None, # Return the section starting with this heading, plus its children
    pred:callable=None, # Extra match criterion, e.g. from `symdef_finder`/`symref_finder`/`ast_finder`, or host-specific flags
)->MsgRows: # Snapshot rows (`id`, `msg_type`, `content`, `out`, `meta`), indexed by id and shown as previews with context rows marked
```

*Find messages in the dialog file matching all the given criteria; for
live results, call
[`Dialog.find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#dialog.find_msgs)*

### Dialog.find_msgs

``` python
def find_msgs(
    re_pattern:str='', # Regex over content (a prompt's reply included), DOTALL+MULTILINE; an invalid regex matches literally
    msg_type:str=None, # Optional limit by type ('code', 'note', 'prompt', or 'raw')
    only_err:bool=False, # Only code messages with error outputs?
    only_exp:bool=False, # Only exported messages (nbdev export directive in content or meta)?
    ids:str='', # Optionally filter by ids (comma-separated str, or list); results are always in dialog order, whatever order the ids are given
    before:int=0, # Also include n messages before each match
    after:int=0, # Also include n messages after each match
    context:int=None, # Messages of context around matches (default 1, or 0 when `headers_only`)
    limit:int=None, # Max matched messages
    use_case:bool=False, # Case-sensitive matching?
    use_regex:bool=True, # Regex matching (else plain substring)?
    headers_only:bool=False, # Only heading notes (an outline view)?
    header_section:str=None, # Return the section starting with this heading, plus its children
    pred:callable=None, # Extra match criterion, e.g. from `symdef_finder`/`symref_finder`/`ast_finder`, or host-specific flags
)->FoundMsgs: # Live messages plus context rows, indexed by id, so results can be edited directly
```

*Find this dialog’s messages matching all the given criteria*

[`Dialog.find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#dialog.find_msgs)
returns the messages themselves, so a search on a held dialog can be
edited in place; wrapping any message list in an ephemeral
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
makes it searchable the same way. A prompt matches on its request or its
reply; an invalid regex matches literally (search text arrives verbatim
from humans); `pred=` takes any extra criterion, the channel hosts pass
their own flag logic through; `header_section` follows note-message
headings; `headers_only` gives an outline. `context` defaults to 1,
since the neighbouring message is usually the explanation of whatever
matched; pass `context=0` for exact hits only:

``` python
test_eq(d.find_msgs('42', context=0), [ask])  # matches the reply text
test_eq(d.find_msgs(r'x\*2', msg_type=scode, context=0), [calc])
test_eq(d.find_msgs(only_err=True, context=0), [bad])
test_eq(len(d.find_msgs(r'x\*2')), 3)  # context defaults to 1: the match plus both neighbours
test_eq(d.find_msgs(headers_only=True), [setup])
test_eq(d.find_msgs(header_section='Setup', context=0), list(d.messages))  # everything under the heading
test_eq(Dialog(d.messages[:3]).find_msgs('42', context=0), [ask])  # an ephemeral wrap makes any message list searchable
fm = d.find_msgs('42', context=0)
fm[ask.id].content = 'Double it, please.'
test_eq(ask.content, 'Double it, please.')  # live objects: the edit landed on the dialog
assert ask.dlg is d  # ...and the wrap above didn't steal the message from its real dialog
test_eq(d.find_msgs('*42*', context=0), [ask])  # an invalid regex falls back to a literal match
test_eq(d.find_msgs(pred=lambda m: m.msg_type==sprompt, context=0), [ask])  # host-specific extra criterion
xd = Dialog(name='exports')
exp1 = xd.mk_message('#| export\ndef f(): pass', msg_type=scode)
exp2 = xd.mk_message('def g(): pass', msg_type=scode)
exp2.meta_exported = True
deep = xd.mk_message('## Deep\nbody under the heading', msg_type=snote)
test_eq(xd.find_msgs(only_exp=True, context=0), [exp1, exp2])
test_eq(xd.find_msgs(header_section='Deep', context=0), [deep])  # matched on the first line only
test_eq(xd.find_msgs(header_section='## Deep', context=0), [deep])  # a '#'-prefixed argument pins the level
test_eq(xd.find_msgs(header_section='# Deep', context=0), [])
```

Filtering by `ids=` still brings the neighbours – the context is why you
looked – and the sample id in the raised error comes from the actual
matches:

``` python
fm = d.find_msgs(ids=calc.id)
test_eq((fm.matched, len(fm)), ({calc.id}, 3))
with expect_fail(TypeError, 'context rows'): fm[0]
test_eq(fm[calc.id], calc)
fm
```

    de618713:n-# Setup
    9271acf1:c:x = 21\nx*2 ⇒ out(103)
    7a9befd3:p-Double it, please.
    > It is **42**.

The function form addresses a *file* and returns
[`MsgRow`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgrow)
snapshots: data to read plus the id to act on, never live objects. The
file was written before the live `ask` was edited above, so the row
still shows the file’s content - the snapshot/live distinction in one
line:

``` python
rows = find_msgs('42', dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', context=0)
test_eq([r.id for r in rows], [ask.id])
test_eq(rows[ask.id].content, 'Double it.')  # the file's snapshot, not the live edit above
assert not isinstance(rows[ask.id], Message) and rows[ask.id].msg_type==sprompt
with expect_fail(TypeError, 'path'): find_msgs('42', dlg=d)  # a live Dialog goes through the method, never dlg=
rows
```

    7a9befd3:p:Double it.
    > It is **42**.

### Message.split

``` python
def split(
    *linenos:int, # Split before each of these 1-based lines
):
```

*Split this message into pieces (returned as
[`Msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgs); the
first keeps its id): one `'\n\n'` is absorbed at each cut (so
[`merge_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#merge_msgs)
restores blank-line-separated content byte-exactly), `meta_attrs`
fields, the cell `meta`, and a leading `#| export` copy to every piece,
attachments follow their references, and unreferenced ones stay on the
first piece*

``` python
sd = Dialog(name='s')
sm = sd.mk_message('#| export\ndef f(): pass\ndef g(): pass', msg_type=scode, meta={'k': 1})
i1,i2 = sm.split(3)
test_eq([m.content for m in sd.messages], ['#| export\ndef f(): pass', '#| export\ndef g(): pass'])
test_eq([m.meta for m in sd.messages], [{'k': 1}, {'k': 1}])  # whole cell meta copies to every piece
i2.meta['k'] = 2  # pieces don't share the dict
test_eq(i1.meta, {'k': 1})
sd.merge_msgs(i1, i2)
test_eq((sd.messages[0].content, sd.messages[0].meta), ('#| export\ndef f(): pass\n\ndef g(): pass', {'k': 1}))
hd = Dialog(name='hoist')
h1, h2 = hd.mk_message('def a(): pass'), hd.mk_message('#| export\ndef b(): pass')
hm = hd.merge_msgs(h1, h2)  # any exported piece exports the merge, via meta
test_eq((hm.content, hm.meta, hm.exported), ('def a(): pass\n\ndef b(): pass', {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}, True))
sd.mk_message('tail', msg_type=snote)
sd.move_msgs(i1, after=sd.messages[-1])
test_eq([m.content[:4] for m in sd.messages], ['tail', '#| e'])
```

``` python
ad = Dialog(name='atts')
at1, at2 = Attachment(b'x', 'text/plain'), Attachment(b'y', 'text/plain')
am = ad.mk_message(f'see attachment:{at1.id}\nplain tail', msg_type=snote, attachments=[at1, at2])
p1, p2 = am.split(2)
test_eq(len(p1.attachments), 2)  # the referenced one, plus the unreferenced one kept on the first piece
test_eq(p2.attachments, [])
jd = Dialog(name='junction')
j = jd.mk_message('a\n\n\nb', msg_type=snote)
j1, j2 = j.split(4)
test_eq((j1.content, j2.content), ('a\n', 'b'))  # one '\n\n' absorbed at the cut: exactly what merge re-inserts
test_eq(jd.merge_msgs(j1, j2).content, 'a\n\n\nb')  # ...so blank-line-separated content round trips byte-exactly
k1, k2 = jd.mk_message('a\n\nb', msg_type=snote).split(3)
test_eq((k1.content, k2.content), ('a', 'b'))
w1, w2 = jd.mk_message('a\n\n\nb', msg_type=snote).split(3)  # cut on the blank line: residue stays on the right
test_eq((w1.content, w2.content), ('a', '\nb'))
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'Exactly one'): jd.move_msgs(w2)
```

## Editing message text

The editing operations run fastcore.tools’ text primitives over a
message’s content, or, with `out=True`, over a prompt’s reply markdown
(assignment re-wraps it through
[`prompt_output`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#prompt_output)).
Only prompts have text-editable output: for a code message’s outputs,
assign `msg.output` directly. The old behavior of editing a prompt
cell’s joined request+reply source is retired. In bulk mode (a list of
ids, or ‘all’), no-ops are dropped from the result but errors are
reported.

The spliced editors inherit `fastcore.tools`’ signatures, so the
toolkit-wide `replace_params` group (declared identically in
`fastcore.editskill`) collapses the same six options in `doc()`
overviews here:

``` python
(tdir/'edit.ipynb').write_bytes((tdir/'demo.ipynb').read_bytes())  # scratch copy: demo.ipynb stays pristine for later sections
set_dlg(tdir/'edit.ipynb')
diff = msg_str_replace(calc.id, 'x = 21', 'x = 40')
assert '-x = 21' in str(diff) and '+x = 40' in str(diff)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'edit.ipynb').msg(calc.id).content, 'x = 40\nx*2')
```

``` python
diff = msg_str_replace(ask.id, '**42**', '**80**', out=True)
assert '+It is **80**.' in str(diff)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'edit.ipynb').msg(ask.id).ai_res, 'It is **80**.')
assert str(msg_str_replace(calc.id, "'42'", "'80'", out=True)).startswith('error:')
assert str(msg_del_lines(setup.id, 1, 1, out=True)).startswith('error:')
bulk = msg_str_replace([setup.id, bad.id], '1/0', 'pass')
test_eq(len(bulk), 2)  # bulk mode reports errors alongside diffs
assert 'error' in bulk[0][1] and '+pass' in bulk[1][1]
```

## Structural search

Text search fights Python syntax: `cfg =` misses `cfg, aux = load()`,
and a loose pattern on a two-letter name floods. The finder trio turns
remold’s structural queries into predicates for `find_msgs(pred=)`:
[`symdef_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#symdef_finder)
matches messages that bind a name in their top-level scope, however
Python spells the binding (tuple unpacking, `for`, `with ... as`,
walrus, imports, `def`/`class`);
[`symref_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#symref_finder)
matches those that read it; and
[`ast_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#ast_finder)
matches an ast-grep pattern. A message that doesn’t parse as Python
never matches, so prose cells exclude themselves.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L469"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


*[`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#find_msgs)

`remold`)*

``` python
fd = Dialog(name='finders')
f1 = fd.mk_message('cfg, aux = load_cfg()', msg_type=scode)
f2 = fd.mk_message('print(render(cfg))', msg_type=scode)
fd.mk_message('cfg is set up above', msg_type=snote)
test_eq(fd.find_msgs(pred=symdef_finder('cfg'), context=0), [f1])
test_eq(fd.find_msgs(pred=symref_finder('cfg'), context=0), [f2])
test_eq(fd.find_msgs(pred=ast_finder('render($_)'), context=0), [f2])
```

## Hash-verified edits

`m.lnhashview()` and `m.exhash()` bring exhash’s stale-context-proof
addressing to a held message;
[`lnhashview_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#lnhashview_msg)/[`msg_exhash`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#msg_exhash)
are their file-transaction twins, taking an id and `dlg=` path.
[`Message.lnhashview`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#message.lnhashview)
is sugar for `view(lnhashs=True)` and accepts the same
`start_line`/`end_line` range; the exhash pair imports `exhash` lazily,
so aidialog carries no hard dependency on it:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L503"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
diff = calc.exhash((lnhash(1, 'x = 21'), 's', '21', '12'))
```

The transactional twins take a message id, resolved through `dlg` like
[`view_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#view_msg)
(the current dialog file when None), and save back to the file
automatically:

``` python
msg_replace_lines(calc.id, new_content='a = 1\na*2')
test_eq(str(lnhashview_msg(calc.id, start_line=2, end_line=2)), f'{lnhash(2, "a*2")}a*2')
diff = msg_exhash(calc.id, (lnhash(1, 'a = 1'), 's', '1', '9'))
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'edit.ipynb').msg(calc.id).content, 'a = 9\na*2')
```

## Working with dialog files

Every function above takes `dlg` as an ipynb path, or None meaning the
current dialog file
([`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg));
each call reads the file fresh, applies, and saves - a transaction. A
held
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
never goes through `dlg=`: its methods are the session surface,
mutations stay in memory, and `dlg.save()` commits
([`cur_dlg()`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#cur_dlg)
opens a fresh session on the current file). The two shapes don’t see
each other mid-flight, so use one at a time per file: save before
switching to functions, reopen after.
[`write_ipynb`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/ipynb.html#write_ipynb)’s
byte-stability keeps the resulting diffs minimal. A few functions below
exist only for the file world:

``` python
set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb')
assert '<prompt' in str(view_dlg())
assert str(summary_dlg()).count('\n')==4  # 4 messages, plus the prompt's reply line
s = str(find_msgs(r'x\*2', msg_type=scode, context=0))
assert s and s.count('\n')==0  # a code row is one preview line (empty would pass a bare count check)
xd.mk_message('', msg_type=sraw, meta=dict(rec_kind='system', rec={}))
assert 'kind="system"' in str(xd.view())  # tagged raws are badged, never shown as ordinary content
```

A `dlg=` path that does not exist raises `FileNotFoundError`, so a bad
path fails loudly in every function here:

``` python
with expect_fail(FileNotFoundError, 'does not exist'): summary_dlg(tdir/'missing.ipynb')
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L543"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### create_dlg

``` python
def create_dlg(
    fname:str, # path for the new ipynb; must not already exist
    source:str='', # source for its first message
    msg_type:str='code', # 'code', 'note', 'prompt', or 'raw'
):
```

*Create a new dialog file containing one message, returning the
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
(with `path_` stamped)*

### add_msg

``` python
def add_msg(
    source:str, # source for the new message
    msg_type:str='code', # 'code', 'note', 'prompt', or 'raw'
    before:str=None, # message or id to insert before
    after:str=None, # message or id to insert after; defaults to the current message (`set_cur_msg`)
    meta:NoneType=None, # Cell metadata, carried verbatim through save/load
    export:bool=False, # Also set the meta `nbdev` export flag? (`meta_exported`)
    dlg:NoneType=None, # An ipynb path (expands `~`); the current dialog file if None
):
```

*Add a new message before or after an existing one (default: after the
current message, else at the end), returning it*

``` python
nm = add_msg('print(9)', after=calc.id)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(nm).content, 'print(9)')
test_eq(del_msgs(nm)[0].content, 'print(9)')
with expect_fail(KeyError, 'no message'): read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(nm)
nd = create_dlg(tdir/'new.ipynb', '# hi', 'note')
test_eq(nd.messages[0].msg_type, snote)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'new.ipynb').msg(nd.messages[0]).content, '# hi')
```

A host’s
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
subclass usually pairs with a
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
subclass declaring extra `meta_attrs`; passing it once via
`set_dlg(cls=)` makes every ambient read construct it:

``` python
class _HostMsg(Message):
    meta_attrs = dict(Message.meta_attrs, starred='starred')
class _HostDlg(Dialog): msg_cls = _HostMsg

set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb', cls=_HostDlg)
starred = add_msg('to star', 'note', meta=dict(starred=True))
assert cur_dlg().msg(starred.id).starred  # promoted to an attribute by the host class
set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb')  # bare set_dlg keeps the class...
assert isinstance(cur_dlg(), _HostDlg)
set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb', cls=Dialog)  # ...replacing it is explicit
assert not isinstance(cur_dlg(), _HostDlg)
del_msgs(starred)
```

With an anchor set, a bare
[`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg)
lands after it, and chaining through each returned message keeps a run
of adds in order. Writing never moves the anchor:

``` python
set_cur_msg(calc)
a = add_msg('a = 1')
b = add_msg('b = 2', after=a)
test_eq(cur_msg().id, calc.id)
test_eq(cur_msgid, calc.id)  # the bare state: importers read it as `dlgskill.cur_msgid`
summary_dlg()
```

An anchor naming a message that isn’t there falls back to appending, so
deleting the message a host last ran never turns a later add into an
error:

``` python
set_cur_msg('gone')
z = add_msg('z = 3')
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').messages[-1].content, 'z = 3')
del_msgs(a, b, z)
set_cur_msg(None)
summary_dlg()
```

An `export=True` shortcut (or an explicit `meta=`) marks the new message
as exported via the meta `nbdev` dict, and the summary shows it as
`[export]`:

``` python
xm = add_msg('def q(): pass', after=calc.id, export=True)
test_eq(xm.meta, {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}})
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(xm).meta_exported, True)
assert ':c[export]:' in xm.preview()
del_msgs(xm)
```

    063e9740:c[export]:def q(): pass

[`update_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#update_msg)
is
[`Message.update`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.update)
as a transaction: addressed by an id you type, applied to the dialog
file, verified by the returned diff of the message’s XML and meta:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L559"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### update_msg

``` python
def update_msg(
    id, # A `Message`, or an id: exact, or unique prefix
    dlg:NoneType=None, # An ipynb path (expands `~`); the current dialog file if None
    mergemeta:dict=None, # `deep_merge` into `meta`; a `None` value deletes its key
    export:bool=None, # Add (True) or remove (False) the nbdev export directive; a content-form line migrates to meta
):
```

*Update a message’s type, meta, or export directive in the dialog file
(see
[`Message.update`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.update))*

A meta-only change is invisible in the message XML, so the diff carries
a `meta:` line too:

``` python
set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb')
print(update_msg(calc.id, export=True))
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(calc.id).meta_exported, True)
print(update_msg(calc.id, mergemeta=dict(nbdev=None)))
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(calc.id).exported, False)
```

    @@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
    -<code id="9271acf1">x = 21
    +<code id="9271acf1" export>x = 21
     x*2</code>
    -meta: {}
    +meta: {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}
    @@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
    -<code id="9271acf1" export>x = 21
    +<code id="9271acf1">x = 21
     x*2</code>
    -meta: {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}
    +meta: {}

``` python
s1, s2 = split_msg(calc.id, 2)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(s2).content, 'x*2')
merge_msgs(s1, s2)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(s1).content, 'x = 21\n\nx*2')
copy_msgs(s1)
pids = paste_msgs(after=s1)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(pids[0].id).content, 'x = 21\n\nx*2')
del_msgs(pids[0].id)
```

    12797ff2:c:x = 21\n\nx*2

Under IPython, the `%%add_msg` magic takes the message body verbatim (no
Python quoting):
`%%add_msg [<path>] before=<id>|after=<id> [code|note|prompt|raw] [export]`.
Keyword spellings (`dlg=`, `msg_type=`) are accepted too, and always win
over bare tokens:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L574"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### add_msg_magic

``` python
def add_msg_magic(
    line, cell
):
```

*Add a new message with the magic body as its source, taken verbatim; a
bare `export` token sets the meta `nbdev` export flag.*

``` python
nm = add_msg_magic(f"note dlg={tdir/'demo.ipynb'} after={calc.id}", 'magic body')
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(nm.id).content, 'magic body')
test_eq(nm.msg_type, 'note')
xm = add_msg_magic(f"code export dlg={tdir/'demo.ipynb'} after={calc.id}", 'def r(): pass')
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(xm.id).meta_exported, True)
```

The `%nbrun` line magic runs code cells from the current notebook
([`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg))
in the running kernel, by cell id prefix. It follows the same grammar as
`%%add_msg`: bare tokens are flag names (`above`, `below`, `all`,
`exported`, `ignore_eval`, `continue_on_error`, `show`) or cell id
prefixes, `k=v` spellings win over bare tokens, a bare line runs every
code cell (like
[`Dialog.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog.execute)),
and `fname=` overrides the notebook for one call. Verbosity follows the
selector: cells named by id run as a notebook cell would
([`fastcore.nbio.run_cell`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#run_cell)
with `store_history=True`, so results display through the kernel’s own
displayhook and a trailing `;` suppresses natively), while bulk-selected
cells (the `above`/`below`/`all`/`exported` expansions) run `silent`
with both streams captured, since they are scaffolding whose output
nobody reads. `show` forces full display for every cell. A failing cell
always surfaces. The shell has already displayed its traceback once, a
bulk cell’s captured streams are re-emitted first, and a
`nbrun: error in cell <id>` line names it. The run then stops without
raising, unless `continue_on_error` moves on. Every run ends with a
`nbrun: N cells ok` summary line, with a failure count when there were
any. Cells run in the kernel’s namespace through user-level channels
only (streams, the display publisher, the shell’s own error display), so
the magic is correct in every kernel. The magic returns a coroutine,
awaited by the async-magic machinery
([`fastcore.aio.enable_async_magics`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/aio.html#enable_async_magics)).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L608"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### load_ipython_extension

``` python
def load_ipython_extension(
    ipython
):
```

*Call self as a function.*

``` python
rd = create_dlg(tdir/'run.ipynb', 'zz = 5')
rm2 = add_msg('zz2 = zz+1', after=rd.messages[0].id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
await nbrun_magic(f"{rm2.id} above fname={tdir/'run.ipynb'}")
test_eq((zz, zz2), (5, 6))
set_dlg(tdir/'run.ipynb')
await nbrun_magic(rd.messages[0].id)
test_eq(zz, 5)
```

    nbrun: 2 cells ok
    nbrun: 1 cell ok

The loop is shell-agnostic: a fresh `InteractiveShell` is a minimal
kernel with its own namespace, and the same code drives it:

``` python
psh = InteractiveShell()
await _run_nb_cells(psh, [rm2.id], tdir/'run.ipynb', above=True)
test_eq((psh.user_ns['zz'], psh.user_ns['zz2']), (5, 6))
bad = add_msg('no_such_name', after=rm2.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
cap = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [bad.id], tdir/'run.ipynb')
assert f'nbrun: error in cell {bad.id}' in cap.getvalue() and 'NameError' in cap.getvalue()
```

    nbrun: 2 cells ok

``` python
noisy = add_msg("print('noisy')", after=rm2.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
target = add_msg("print('target')", after=noisy.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
cap = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [target.id], tdir/'run.ipynb', above=True)
out = cap.getvalue()
assert 'target' in out and 'noisy' not in out and '---' not in out
assert 'nbrun: 4 cells ok' in out
cap = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [target.id], tdir/'run.ipynb', above=True, show=True)
assert 'noisy' in cap.getvalue()
cap = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [], tdir/'run.ipynb', all=True)
allout = cap.getvalue()
assert str(bad.id) in allout and 'noisy' not in allout and 'NameError' in allout
assert 'nbrun: 4 cells ok, 1 failed' in allout
out
```

    'target\nnbrun: 4 cells ok\n'

A failing run stops at the bad cell without raising, since the shell has
already displayed the traceback once and re-raising would show it twice.
The captured streams of a failing bulk cell are re-emitted first, stderr
included, which is otherwise swallowed like stdout. The
`nbrun: error in cell` line then names the culprit:

``` python
after_bad = add_msg('should_not_run = 1', after=bad.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
warner = add_msg("import sys; sys.stderr.write('warn-noise\\n'); zz3 = 1", after=rm2.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
cap, cerr = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap), redirect_stderr(cerr): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [], tdir/'run.ipynb', all=True)
assert 'should_not_run' not in psh.user_ns
assert psh.user_ns['zz3'] == 1 and 'warn-noise' not in cerr.getvalue()
```

`continue_on_error` presses on past the failure, and the summary line
counts both:

``` python
cap2 = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap2): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [], tdir/'run.ipynb', all=True, stop=False)
test_eq(psh.user_ns['should_not_run'], 1)
cap2.getvalue().splitlines()[-1]
```

    'nbrun: 6 cells ok, 1 failed'

A bare line goes through the magic’s grammar as an empty selection,
which
[`nbrun_magic`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#nbrun_magic)
turns into `all`:

``` python
cap3 = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap3): await nbrun_magic(f"fname={tdir/'run.ipynb'}")
assert re.search(r'nbrun: \d+ cells ok', cap3.getvalue())
cap3.getvalue().splitlines()[-1]
```

Bulk selections follow the `eval` cascade
([`fastcore.nbio.select_cells`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#select_cells)):
an `#| eval: false` cell drops out of `all`-style runs, though naming it
by id still runs it. The `ignore_eval` flag disables the filtering
wholesale, and the retired `skip_noeval` flag names its replacement:

``` python
ed = create_dlg(tdir/'ev.ipynb', 'ran = 1')
en = add_msg('#| eval: false\nnever = 1', after=ed.messages[0].id, dlg=tdir/'ev.ipynb')
await nbrun_magic(f"fname={tdir/'ev.ipynb'}")
assert 'never' not in get_ipython().user_ns              # bulk runs follow the eval cascade
await nbrun_magic(f"ignore_eval fname={tdir/'ev.ipynb'}")
test_eq(never, 1)                                        # ignore_eval: Jupyter-style run-all
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'skip_noeval'): nbrun_magic('skip_noeval')
```
